_: Dates checked by hand, overriding what the extractor guessed.
The extractor reads a year out of Michael's prose, and prose about old
equipment is full of years belonging to other things: the price list a
figure came from, the issue of the Bolex Reporter that announced a motor,
the camera an accessory was made to fit. A wrong date is worse than no
date on a page people use to identify what they own, so every year the
extractor proposed was read back against its sentence, and the ones it
year: null means the prose states no date for this object, whatever
numbers appear in it. Each entry says what the sentence actually said.

cinelac-film-preserver.note: The 1942 is the date of an article recommending it on microfilm, not of the product. Advertised through the 1940s, undated.

l-1.note: The 1947 belongs to the later model of the L-8 camera. The case is described only as late 1940s, introduced 'shortly after'.

eye-level-focuser-early.note: 'Introduced in late 1948 or early 1949.' Michael would not pick between them, so neither does this.

ambol-evn-pan-tripod.note: 'The Evn-Pan was introduced in early 1946.' Missed because of the word early.

eye-level-focus.note: 'This updated version appeared in 1949', standard on the Deluxe and Standard from 1950.

american-bolex-norwood-light-meter.note: 'In 1948, the American Bolex Company began to manufacture and distribute the Norwood Director.'

mst.note: 'Perfectone modified their sync motor in 1967.' That modification is the MST.
